newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Maystadt not seeking new term as Belgian FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Maystadt not seeking new term as Belgian FinMin.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said he would not seek another term in office after the end of the current government in 1999.

"It is correct that I am not asking to head the finance ministry again after the end of the government's normal term in 1999," he told Belgian newspaper De Standaard in an interview published on Friday.
Maystadt, a 48-year-old French-speaking christian-democrat, will have been in office for 11 years by 1999.

"My goal has always been clear: I want Belgium to be among the frontrunners to enter European monetary union in 1999. As soon as Belgium has passed the test, I am open for other things," he said. He gave few clues as to what he would do after 1999.

Persistent rumours have said that Maystadt, already chairman of the powerful Interim Committee of the International Monetary Fund, might take over as IMF managing director from Michel Camdessus, whose term ends in 2000.

Maystadt has not ruled out a top European Union post, but equally might stay in Belgium to help his native francophone Walloon region, much of it a post-industrial age wasteland, recover from its economic troubles.
